prompt_text:

Two cases stand out in the sample: Attabira accounts for Rs 10.30 lakh (91.2%) of the planned cost of abandoned markets and fairs works [d1-22655] and has the only agriculture activity marked abandoned [d1-19912].

results.question: Mendarajpur - show me what the analysis found.
results.tagged:
Mendarajpur recorded 623 planned activities [p-gp-275075-A1], of which 421 (67.6%) had no cost attached [p-gp-275075-A2]. Against a recorded plan of Rs 3.19 crore [p-gp-275075-A3], it spent Rs 1.32 crore on planned activities [p-gp-275075-A5]. That was 41.2% of planned cost, close to the middle value of 42.0% in the 20-Gram-Panchayat sample [p-gp-275075-A6].

Of the Rs 1.88 crore gap between plan and spending, Rs 1.47 crore (78.5%) was on activities with no sanctioning authority recorded [d1-32143]. In a separate breakdown of the same gap, activities recorded under output Code 101 accounted for Rs 1.58 crore (84.0%) [d1-32083]. The largest annual gaps were in 2025-2026 (Rs 74.56 lakh) and 2023-2024 (Rs 62.24 lakh) [d1-32222]. Across sectors, the largest gaps against plan were in water conservation (Rs 40.75 lakh) and women and child development (Rs 30.86 lakh) [d1-32001]. Among activities with sanctions on file, spending was Rs 40.44 lakh below sanction, with the largest gaps in sanitation (Rs 9.04 lakh) and drinking water (Rs 8.88 lakh) [d1-32002].

The grant plans show a different split: nearly all of the Rs 59.89 lakh in planned tied grants was for drinking water (Rs 30.27 lakh) and sanitation (Rs 28.87 lakh) [d1-31994]. Of the Rs 2.60 crore in planned untied grants, the largest allocations were for village infrastructure (Rs 1.04 crore) and the Water Sufficient Village theme (Rs 58.37 lakh) [d1-31974].

At the next review, reconcile cashbook payments with activity records and check the status of older works [d2-01861][p-gp-275075-E5]. Cashbook payments linked to planned activities totalled Rs 1.23 crore; the linked share rose from 2.7% to 53.2% across the six years, which does not by itself show that spending rose [d2-01861]. No works were marked completed [p-gp-275075-E2], and 66 works planned in 2022-2023 or earlier were still marked ongoing despite recorded spending of Rs 88.40 lakh (83.0% of their planned cost) [p-gp-275075-E5]. Photo evidence is on file for 107 activities and can be checked against the work records where available [p-gp-275075-E4].
